agent.problem: Non-opening story cards 3, 7, 9 and 15 contain three, three, four and three sentences respectively, counting the quoted sentences on card 7. Each exceeds the two-sentence maximum.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

agent.problem: The distractor “Whether God will allow it” is too close to “Whether Jesus is willing.” Both can be understood as uncertainty about divine consent, so a baker could reasonably defend the distractor as correct.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

agent.problem: Too many choices depend on luck rather than the earlier cards: how Jesus heals (6), the immediate timing (8), the warning's content (10), the priest and Moses details (11), the offering's purpose (12), and whether the man obeys (14) are not inferable from their setups. Six of the ten choice cards are discovery questions, so most choices are not informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

agent.problem: Neither blank can be reasoned out from the earlier cards, which have not introduced the priest, Moses or the cleansing instructions. The blanks ask for wording and details the baker has not seen rather than meaning supported by the setup.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
